Hi Claire — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can model costs for the pilot: 

Recap / assumptions we captured on the call:
- Expected baseline: ~120M tokens / month for customer-facing product search (95% generation, 5% embeddings for rerank).
- Peak concurrency: ~200 qps during promos (bursty but short-lived).
- Target budget range you mentioned: $600k–$900k ARR (you said you wanted guidance on effective $/1M tokens for planning).

Open items we need from you to finalize pack and pricing: 
1) Average prompt + response size (characters or example prompts) — helps convert to tokens.
2) Percent of requests you expect to be served from deterministic cached responses (e.g., canned product descriptions) vs fully-generated outputs.
3) Any regulatory requirement that forces on-prem or VPC-only (affects discounting and architecture).

What I committed to do:
- Convert your sample prompt set to tokens (we'll attach a per-prompt token estimate).
- Run two cost models: (A) conservative — assume no cache; (B) optimistic — 30% full-response cache + prefix caching on repeated queries.
- Recommend a target $/1M tokens and suggested tiering for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Attachments: FastRetail_MonthlyUsage_estimate_May2029.csv (we'll update this after you share sample prompts)

Next steps: If you can reply with the two items above (prompt examples + estimated percent cached), I’ll send an annotated cost model and a proposed pilot SOW.

1) Prompt/examples: attaching a small sample file (see inline below) — most prompts average ~1,400 characters (product title + 2 short bullets + user intent). We don’t have tokens measured yet; hope you can convert.
2) Cache behavior: around 20–30% of traffic is deterministic (product descriptions, static FAQs) and could be served from a full-response cache. Another ~25% shows high prefix overlap (same product title + user modifier), so prefix/KV caching sounds promising.
3) Compliance: Hosted is fine for pilot; if we move to enterprise rollout we may require VPC.

Budget context: Our finance owner gave me a target of ~ $750k ARR for the pilot year (includes infra + usage + support). We wanted to know what effective $/1M tokens buys under conservative vs cached scenarios.

Questions: Does Redwood bill by characters or tokens? Also, does using a cache reduce billed tokens or only latency/compute? That part is still confusing to our procurement team.

Subject: Re: Post-call debrief: metering & cost — tokens vs characters vs cache

Claire — thanks for the details, very helpful. Below is a concise explanation you can share with procurement + the numbers we’ll model next. I kept it non-technical but precise.

Short answers first:
- Redwood bills by tokens (model input tokens + output tokens). We do not bill by raw character count.
- Request count (API calls) is not billed as a primary unit for text generation (we do have per-request limits and rate-based throttling, but your charge is primarily token-based).
- Caching can reduce billed tokens only if the cached response is served without invoking the model. Prefix/KV caching reduces compute and often reduces billed tokens in practice because less decoding is required — the exact savings depend on whether the cache can fully satisfy the request and on your prompt/response distribution.

How to map characters -> tokens (practical rule of thumb):
- For English product-text, assume ~3.5–4.5 characters per token on average. So your 1,400-character prompt is roughly 300–400 tokens (we will run your sample through the model tokenizer and give exact counts).

Example billing scenarios (we will attach a spreadsheet with line items):
- Baseline (no cache): 120M tokens/month -> at $1,050 per 1M tokens = $126,000 / month (~$1.512M ARR).
- Partial cache (30% full-response + prefix savings for another 25%): Effective tokens billed ~ (120M * 0.45) = 54M tokens/month -> at $1,050 per 1M = $56,700 / month (~$680.4k ARR).
- Optimistic cache (50% full-response): Effective billed tokens ~60M -> $63k / month (~$756k ARR).

Notes on caching behavior vs billing (more detail):
- Full-response cache: if a request is identical to a cached entry, we can serve from the cache without invoking the model runtime. In that case, you are not billed model tokens for that request (we may surface a small CDN/edge serving charge if using Private CDN — included in enterprise SOW).
- Prefix/KV cache: this caches internal transformer KV state for repeated prefixes. It reduces computation because the model does not re-run the prefix tokens; billed tokens are effectively reduced because fewer tokens are decoded/attended to. Savings scale with how often customers reuse prefixes (search queries with similar product titles are a great candidate).
- Edge cases: If you alter system instructions or user modifiers each request (even slightly), prefix cache hit rates drop and savings are lower. We’ll instrument hit rates in the pilot so you can see real billed-token reductions tied to cache hit percentages.

Next steps (what you’ll receive from us):
1) Tokenized sample prompts + per-prompt token counts (by model family).
2) A 3-scenario cost model (baseline / partial-cache / optimistic) with monthly and annualized totals and a recommended pilot tier.
3) Draft SOW with pilot length, expected usage bands, and proposed blended $/1M token rate + 10% pilot credit per Marissa’s suggestion.

If that sounds good I’ll send the spreadsheet by EOD and we can set a 30-minute follow-up early next week to walk procurement through the numbers.

Thanks again — I’ll copy Marissa on the deliverables.
